claims.text: The magnetocaloric response of as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloys is governed by composition-dependent changes in transition temperature or response amplitude.
Hysteresis in these alloys is governed by composition-dependent changes in transition temperature or response amplitude.
Systematic variation of composition can optimize the magnetocaloric response.
The proposed intervention is systematic variation of composition.
The intervention is to be evaluated during low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Transition temperature or response amplitude acts as the structural mediator.
Composition-dependent changes in transition temperature or response amplitude constitute the proposed mechanism.
Systematic composition variation is predicted to produce an optimized magnetocaloric response relative to an unoptimized as-deposited baseline.
Systematic composition variation is predicted to reduce hysteresis relative to an unoptimized as-deposited baseline.
The predictions are intended to hold for rare-earth-free, mechanically stable, low-cost materials that enable rapid heat exchange and limit hysteretic losses.
The exact relationship among composition, transition temperature, and response amplitude is not fully understood.
Finding no significant correlation between composition and either transition temperature or response amplitude would falsify the hypothesis.
